# Owned VST3 initial-value qualification fixture

Independent MIT OR Apache-2.0 adaptation of the existing Mondrian sidechain fixture and its pinned vst3-rs Gain template. Its new component/controller CIDs, MIV1 state and dedicated package do not change historical fixture identities. LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE retain the pinned binding/runtime notices. The existing generated SDK and official provenance remain unchanged; PROVENANCE.json binds the actual seed and SDK bytes. This is a test DLL, not a third-party compatibility result or shipped plugin.

Build centrally (not executed by the author):
`cargo build --locked --manifest-path crates/mondrian-audio/tests/fixtures/vst3-initial-values/Cargo.toml --target-dir target/vst3-initial-values-fixture --message-format=json`

Set `MONDRIAN_VST3_INITIAL_VALUES_TEST_PLUGIN` to the exact freshly built DLL. Run each `processor_isolation::vst3_worker::initial_parameter_values_tests::*` selector separately with `--exact --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` through the frozen Job runner. Bind DLL/test executable/source hashes. Each of the five tests has one libtest summary, with no nested libtest. No native run has been performed by the author.

Stereo main input/output, no auxiliary/event buses, gain DSP, zero latency/tail. Canonical state prefix: MIV1/version1/f64 gain/u32 mode, twenty bytes. Actual SDK state getter audit extends component stream to24bytes (real Process call count) and controller stream to44bytes (metadata/value query counts, setter count, last observed value, sticky wrong-control-thread bit). The host envelope still owns two separate streams; production never parses this fixture state. DSP applies native queue points as step changes at their actual sample offsets, with bounded work and no fixture DSP allocation.

Mode0 produces no restart. Restored modes1–12 use real component-handler callbacks on the initialization/control thread: mode1 pure4; mode2 mixed12; mode3 schema16; mode4 NaN; mode5 normalized1.25; mode6 repeated same-bit4 during getter; mode7 unadmitted ID99; mode8 metadata refusal; mode9 real Begin/Value/End author callbacks during getter; mode10 oversized count1025; mode11 count-1; mode12 missing count0. Controller read faults arm ONLY via a real IMessage on the component/controller connection from native setProcessing(true), after loaded metadata validation. There is no host plugin-name exception, environment switch, filesystem diagnostic or synthetic DSP oracle. Pure4 initial callbacks originate from actual setComponentState/setState, while state getters retain independently observed native counters.

Mode13 keeps the same MIV1/version1/twenty-byte configuration and initial pure4 callbacks. After the existing native `setProcessing(true)` connection message arms the controller, each valid control-thread `setParamNormalized(0, finite 0..=1)` emits a real `restartComponent(4)` and returns its actual status (or `kResultFalse` if the handler is absent). Invalid setters and unarmed setters emit no new restart; getters do not manufacture mode13 callbacks. Existing setter/query/Process counters and the getter's last-observed value let the host distinguish queued DSP delivery from real deferred controller service. This is an owned late-notification stimulus, not MDA compatibility, Runtime handoff or graceful-exit qualification; modes0–12 and the audit layouts remain unchanged.

Mode14 is an independent initial input-origin control. It retains the same MIV1/version1/twenty-byte configuration and component24/controller44-byte audit layouts. During controller `setComponentState`/`setState`, the first mode14 restore on that controller instance sets its own gain to `.75` and calls the actual `IComponentHandler::performEdit(0, .75)` once, without Begin/End, restart or getter callbacks. Restore reentry during the callback refuses without another notification; completed restores on the same controller return the cached actual result, including failure, without replay. No handler means refusal and leaves the notification unattempted. A fresh controller has a fresh notification. Subsequent getters report `.75` until an explicit setter changes the controller value. This one-shot is only fixture stimulus, not host ownership or delivery authority. The component independently restores the gain supplied in its own state (for example `.375`) and remains at that value until its existing real Process consumes a parameter input point; the fixture never mirrors the controller callback into DSP gain. Native getters/state capture do not flush or advance DSP. Modes0–13, class identities and all state/audit byte layouts remain unchanged. This control supplies a legal restore-time Value-only callback for the separately qualified initial-COM consumption path; adding it alone does not qualify that host path.

Modes16–20 retain the original pure4 callbacks during both restore entry points, so the existing initial handshake can finish. Only an armed, valid main/control-thread `setParamNormalized(0, finite 0..=1)` with an actual component handler makes one shared late-info state visible and calls `restartComponent(16)`, returning its real result. Mode16 leaves all admitted metadata fields unchanged; mode17 changes the normalized default from `.5` to `.625`; mode18 changes `stepCount` from0 to4; mode19 changes flags from `kCanAutomate` to `kNoFlags`; mode20 changes only the title from `Gain` to `Gain Updated`. Short title, units and unit ID keep their original values. Arming alone, invalid/unarmed setters and getters do not manufacture these late callbacks or metadata drift. Each subsequent valid armed setter can produce a newer actual16 suffix; either restore entry point resets the late-info state. Modes0–15, CIDs/COM interfaces, the twenty-byte MIV1 configuration and component24/controller44-byte audit layouts remain unchanged. These are host admission/refusal stimuli, not a claim that structural metadata drift is supported.

The tests check actual worker factory/Enter/reload implementations and SDK objects in the lab libtest. Their local DLL controls do not alone qualify product-helper dispatch, scoped-lane threading, a third-party plugin, runtime4 support, GUI workflows, real-time deadlines or cross-platform compatibility. Root must separately rerun the retained actual product-helper external VST3 case and existing configuration/author/state/resource regressions. Existing exact-cohort exhaustion tests cover the atomic saturation boundary; this fixture does not attempt billions of callbacks to reach it.
